articleTitle: Emi from hard and soft switched power electronic converters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper summarises an experiment developed to show the difference in EMI emitted by a hard- or soft-switched converter. The experiment was of a comparative nature. Both the development of the converters and measurement of their EMI is discussed. Both conducted and field induced EMI were measured. The soft-switched converter (auxiliary resonant commutated pole converter) shows big reductions in all EMI along with the benefits of lower losses and possible higher switching frequencies. The use of soft-switching techniques instead of conventional hard-switched topologies are therefore preferable in new designs.

articleTitle: Scheduling of a cogeneration system in response to real-time pricing
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Innovative electricity tariffs provide one of the most important Demand-Side Management (DSM) alternatives [1],[2],[3]. Eskom has introduced a pilot project aimed at developing and introducing a Real-time Pricing (RTP) tariff to its customers [4]. The potential electricity cost savings that this tariff will have on the cogeneration industry will be modelled. Industries with the availability of cogeneration plants are in the advantageous position of managing their generation in accordance with the utility's supply and electricity tariff. This article deals with the basic considerations that must be brought into account when scheduling cogeneration by the industry. The effects of this tariff on a cogeneration plant, specifically on the rescheduling, of not only the cogeneration of the industry, but also on the steam generation and usage are an important consideration for the plant engineers. The model takes into account the specific configuration of the cogeneration process. The model is set up for two different cogeneration configurations. Together with the utility they make up the electricity supply to the industry. If the industry only has one specific cogeneration plant, the input variables to the other plant in the model need to be set to zero.

articleTitle: A computational approach to the analysis of transient and steady-state processes in a generic single pulse high frequency resonant converter
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In the article the processes in a generic single pulse high frequency resonant converter is discussed and investigated The detailed mathematical and computational analysis is carried out and it is compared with experimental results. A good agreement between theory and experiment is observed for all modes of the converter operation, illustrating that this type of converter can be analysed without recourse to extensive numerical computer network simulation packages.

articleTitle: Active snubber for high power igbt modules
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents an integrated active snubber (IACS) to be used with IGBT modules in power converters, applied in utility devices. The IACS is a compound component, consisting of all active and passive components necessary to change a hard-switched converter into a soft-switched converter, i.e. the auxiliary resonant commutated pole (ARCP) converter. The IACS mounts directly onto standard IGBT modules. Although the IACS does not provide perfect soft switching, the switching losses are reduced such that IGBT's can be used at their maximum current and voltage ratings and frequencies of up to 20 kHz.

articleTitle: An autonomous single-phase induction generator using pwm inverter as static var source
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents a split-phase induction generator employing a sinusoidal pulse width modulation (PWM) inverter connected across the auxiliary winding as a static var source. This scheme has the advantage of using the magnitude modulation and the phase angle control of the inverter to regulate and keep the output voltage and frequency constant. The scheme is analyzed using system equations derived from an equivalent circuit based on d-q-o transformation in stationary reference frame. The equations are expressed in terms of flux linkages, and the magnetic saturation of the magnetizing path is modeled by expressing the reciprocal of the instantaneous magnetizing inductance as a function of saturated air gap (magnetizing) flux linkages. The final results are compared with those measured on a practical machine.

articleTitle: Rate-1/2 trellis coding for Q2PSK operating on the rician fading channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of trellis coding on multi-dimensional signal space for the newly developed Four-Dimensional Quadrature-Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (Q2PSK) modulation strategy. Two low-complexity convolutional coding schemes are proposed, the first being a true half rate convolutional coder for Q2PSK and the second, a hybrid half rate convolutional-block coder to be utilised in a (Constant Envelope (CE)Q2PSK system configuration. The encoding and decoding configurations of both the systems are structured in such a way that they can easily be realised by standard components available in the communications industry. The bit error rate performance of the proposed coding schemes, assuming coherent detection, perfect carrier and time synchronisation on the non-frequency selective Rician fading channel, are studied by means of simulation. Furthermore, the benefits of the use of channel state information in conjunction with maximum-likelihood Viterbi decoding are also considered.

articleTitle: Modelling of a fin-fan cooler system with variable speed drives
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the development of a global model for a Fin-Fan Cooler System (FFCS). A FFCS is an air-cooled heat exchanger (ACHE) including the fan drive equipment. The goal of the modelling was to estimate the effect of variable airflow, obtained by variable speed drives (VSDs), on both the heat transfer rate and power consumption of the system. The effect of VSDs is compared to the normal practice of fan on/off switching.

articleTitle: Prediction and analysis of the behavior of squirrel-cage induction machine using coupled magnetic circuit model
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper contributes to the search for a method to accurately model, predict and analyze stray load losses and parasitic torque in squirrel-cage induction machines. The concept of coupled magnetic circuit and winding function are applied to fully modeled the machine, including the rotor bars, taking into account all harmonics (space and saturation). No transformation is required in solving the resulting set of differential equations. An analytical solution method, without loss of generality or any information and which is valid for any operating condition is presented. The model predicts the behavior of the machine based on the actual rotor bar resistance and inductance values and as well determines the actual rotor bar and end-ring currents. The application of the model to the prediction of stray load losses and parasitic torque of an experimental machine is demonstrated. Saturation and second order effects such as skin effect are duly accounted for.

articleTitle: Voltage drop effects depending on different customer feeder connections
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper examines the effect on voltage drop of the way in which single phase customers are connected to the supply feeder. In the past only the balancing of customer connections on the phases was regarded as significant. Several case studies are analysed from which conclusions may be drawn. The bi-phase topology is shown to be a promising alternative to conventional three phase systems.

articleTitle: Guest Editorial CDMA Technology: Changing the face of wireless access
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The world is currently in the midst of a revival phase with computers and communications some of the main drivers of this revival. Although this general statement is not surprising, the specific influence that it has on the lives of the Electrical and Electronic engineering fraternity as well as the world as a whole can only be appreciated by contemplating the size of the industry and its impact on our lives. For instance, the electronics industry is currently the the worlds third largest industrial sector by revenue and 12 of the world's top 50 industrial companies operate in the Electrical, Electronic and Computer industries. What is even more important in terms of this special issue of the Transactions on CDMA Technology is that six of the top 10 Electronics companies in the world are involved in the wireless access business in some form or another. Clearly the business of wireless access is becoming increasingly important in world terms, but perhaps even more importantly, in terms of the development of countries like South Africa.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of CDMA/QPSK systems with nonlinear channel using decision feedback equalizers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper proposes an improvement method for the performance characteristics of quadriphase phase-shift-keyed code-divisoin multiple-access (CDMA/QPSK) system with nonlinear channel such as the satellite repeater which consists of traveling-wave tube (TWT). Two adaptive decision feedback equalizers are used to improve the system performance degraded by the nonlinear channel. From calculation results, it is shown that the degradations are improved considerably.

articleTitle: An M-ary spread spectrum system for CDMA communications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: By using an M-ary spread spectrum technique employing “composite” sequences generated by linear feedback shift registers, robust and bandwidth-efficient CDMA communications can be achieved. A threshold decision scheme whereby erasures as well as errors are declared facilitates detection of poor or marginal channel conditions. By combining the multiple-sequence modulation technique and a Reed-Solomon error correcting code, plus incorporating an informationless sequence of the same period in quadrature with the information-bearing sequence, carrier recovery, spreading sequence synchronization, and block code synchronization can all be achieved jointly. Individual symbols can be detected using efficient Hadamard transforms. Also, the system can easily be made to be “downward compatible” with “conventional” spread spectrum schemes.

articleTitle: Band allocation in CDMA satellite mobile networks with heterogeneous traffic sources
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper we attempt to model the performance of a LEO satellite system with “m” classes of traffic source (heterogeneous services). Each class is defined by different resource and performance requirements, characterized by different bit rates on the uplink and downlink, and different QoS parameters. The CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) multiple access scheme is used and a mobility model is adopted to represent the relative motion of mobile terminals over the satellite spot beams. We investigate the blocking behavior of each traffic class in the network and consider the impact of sub-optimal re-distribution of band resources between the uplink and downlink. A software for the simulation of LEO system has been developed and the results from simulation study of a three traffic class example are shown.

articleTitle: Pwm switching strategy with reduced harmonic injection for buck converters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper demonstrates that the ripple voltage produced on the load side by a single-phase AC-DC converter has the effect of injecting odd current harmonics into the supply side, which the conventional selective harmonic elimination (SHE) and natural sinusoidal PWM-control strategies are unable to eliminate or reduce. It is shown that the switching function of the conventional SHE-control strategy has to be modified if these supply side harmonics are to be eliminated or reduced in the case of buck-type converters. Possible application areas of the proposed switching strategy include DC drives, especially those fed from single-phase overhead supplies, drive systems employing low cost microcontrollers, and AC-DC converters providing DC link voltage for high power inverter-fed AC traction drives. Simulated and experimental results are included to validate analytical results.

articleTitle: Using MEM to describe CDMA multiple access interference
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The Maximum Entropy Method (MEM) is used to evaluate and characterize the Multiple Access Interference (MAI) of a direct sequence Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) system. The MAI distribution is derived and compared with the general assumption that the MAI random variable tends to a Gaussian random variable (this assumption is commonly known as the Gaussian Assumption). The influence of the number of users, K, the spreading sequence length, N, and fading on the MAI are investigated. Further, by using the Minimum Relative Entropy Method (MREM), which is related to the MEM, the discrimination information (relative entropy) between the MAI distribution and an equivalent Gaussian distribution is examined. To investigate the influence of fading on the MAI, a Nakagami-m fading channel model is considered. By altering the parameter m of the Nakagami-m distribution, the degree of fading can be varied, from no fading to severe fading. As input to MEM power moments are computed to calculate the MAI distribution.

articleTitle: A combined coherent carrier recovery and decision-directed delay-lock-loop scheme for DS/SSMA communication systems employing complex spreading sequences
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The majority of papers on code synchronization loop design for DSSS communication systems concentrate on noncoherent schemes employing binary spreading sequences. These loop structures comprise early and late arm structures with squaring devices which are very prone to arm imbalance effects. In this paper a combined coherent carrier recovery and Decision-Directed Delay-Lock-Loop (DD-DLL) synchronization scheme for a DSSS communication system is proposed. The novelty of the technique lies in the fact that it extends the structure proposed by de Gaudenzi et al [1] to enable synchronisation of systems employing both binary and complex spreading sequences. Typical advantages include features such as less sensitivity to arm imbalance problems due to the elimination of squaring devices, improved tracking capability and simplified hardware by requiring only two correlators in stead of four in the DLL structure. The simplified loop structures is the direct result of the novel use of difference signals in both the spreading, demodulation/despreading and DLL processes, leading to the elimination of unwanted cross product interference terms when employing complex spreading sequences. The loop response is analysed analytically and its performance verified through computer simulation in the presence of AWGN and typical non-stationary channel effects, employing both binary as well as a relatively new family of complex Linearly and Non-Linearly Root-of-Unity (L- and NL-RU) filtered spreading sequences, including a recen tly introduced subclass of Analytical Bandlimited Complex (ABC) spreading sequences [2].

articleTitle: Low Rate coding and Diversity for Cellular CDMA
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper considers the performance of direct sequence cellular Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) with low rate convolutional coding and diversity. The communications channel is assumed to be multipath faded, and modeled as a discrete set of Nakagami faded paths. The Nakagami fading distribution has been shown to fit empirical results more generally than other distribution [1]. New analytical results to evaluate the probability of error for the receiver terminals studied in this work are presented. The analytical expressions to calculate the average error rate make us of the Gaussian assumption. Numerical results reveal that, for non-diversity receivers, Nakagami fading is very hostile to a CDMA system, reducing the capacity substantially. However, with the use of RAKE reception, interleaving and convolutional coding, the average error rate can be reduced dramatically, allowing for reliable communications.

articleTitle: Multilevel multiuser detection system in a multi-cell MFSK/FH-CDMA environment
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper proposes a multiuser detection system in a multi-cell M-ary Frequency Shift Keying (MFSK)/frequency hopping (FH)-Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) environment, in which the channel model is an OR-channel and in the reverse link. We have proposed a multiuser detection system in a single cell [2]. However, this system is not adequate to detect multiuser in a multi-cell environment. Therefore, we propose a multiuser detection system based on 3 level OR decision with two thresholds. The proposed detection system can delete inter-cell interference as well as intra-cell interference, receive the weakened desired signal and reject the false alarm. Computer simulation shows the performance improvement.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of some basic ARQ SCHEMES in the presence of multiple user interference
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper investigates the throughput efficiencies of some well known ARQ schemes when used for error control on channels where Multiple User Interference (MUI) plays a very significant role, such as Code Division Multiple Access or CDMA channels. The paper also investigates the reliability of some Hamming codes used as error detecting codes in the ARQ schemes on CDMA channels. All of the results are presented as functions of the number of users present in the CDMA systems considered. Fritchman channel models of the MUI present in a CDMA environment are used to calculate parameters such as the undetected error probability of the Hamming codes used for error detection in the ARQ schemes. The throughput of the various ARQ schemes are also calculated for random error channels such as the Binary Symmetric Channel (BSC) and compared to that for the channels with MUI. All of the results show that the ARQ schemes considered all have higher throughput efficiencies on the channels with MUI when compared to channels with random errors at an average bit error rate comparable to that of the channels with MUI. In order to achieve reliability in ARQ schemes used on channels with MUI, codes with shorter block lenghts seem to improve the reliability substantially when compared to longer block lengths. In this paper we are comparing block lengths of 255 and 1023 bits. The results indicate that the ARQ schemes are more reliable on channels with MUI when compared to channels with completely random errors.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of a multidimensional Q2PSK frame synchronisation strategy in fading mobile radio channels
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper considers extended performance analysis of a multidimensional correlation frame synchronisation strategy and its applicability to four-dimensional modulation schemes, with specific reference to Quadrature-Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PSK). This synchronisation strategy is ideally suited for burst mode mobile digital communications, which require frame alignment and where the bits are subjected to multipath fading or other disturbances. A formal description of the multidimensional frame synchronisation procedure, considering the state transition diagram, the choice of complex correlation sequences, and finally the synchroniser algorithm are given. This paper compares the performance of the multidimensional frame synchronisation strategy in a typical Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PSK communication system, to that of conventional two-dimensional techniques, on a fading multipath V/UHF radio channel.

articleTitle: Comparison of complex spreading sequences based on filtering methods and mean square correlation characteristics
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents an overview and comparison of some of the known families of polyphase sequences for Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum Multiple Access (DS/SSMA) communication systems. A comparison between Zadoff Chu (ZC), Oppermann & Vucetic (OV), and Constant-Envelope Root-of-Unity (CE-RU) filtered Generalized-Chirp-Like (GCL) sequences is presented including the special class of Analytical Bandlimited Complex (ABC) spreading sequences. This comparison is based on aperiodic correlation characteristics rather than traditionally discussed parameters like periodic, even, and odd correlations and the emphasis is based on practical considerations rather than rigorous mathematical derivation as found in the most of the literature. This paper is unique in the sense that it also presents the effect of filtering on polyphase sequences by using proper filtering methods. The said classes of the sequences are filtered by using a Nyquist filter, and a Constant Envelope Root-of-Unity (CE-RU) filtering process. It is shown that RU filter performance is better than that of Nyquist filter and also provides a substantial processing gain over Nyqiust filtered sequences. This paper also examines the performance of three classes of sequences using the criterion of mean square values of aperiodic cross-correlation.

Author Keywords: Constant-Envelope Root-of-Unity filtered Double Side Band (CE-RU DSB)

articleTitle: Design and performance evaluation of a turbo/walsh-hadamard coded QPSK DS/CDMA system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents the design of a turbo encoding scheme with embedded Walsh-Hadamard (WH) codewords, and a suitable decoder structure based on an iterative decoding technique, akin to the work on “superorthogonal” turbo codes presented by Pehkonen and Komulainen. The main contributions of this paper are a detailed design of the turbo decoder structure required to perform the required decoding steps, and theoretical analysis to provide upper bounds on bit error rate performance. Attention is focused on an 8-state rate 2/64 coded QPSK DS/CDMA system, in agreement with the rate offered by the IS-95 coding scheme. The bit error rate performance of the proposed iterative turbo coded DS/CDMA system operating on the AWGN channel is studied by means of simulation and compared to that of a DS/CDMA system employing the IS-95 front-end coder for the reverse link channel. Both single and multi-user system performance are considered.

articleTitle: An Overview of Space Division Multiple Access Techniques in Cellular Systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the basic principles of Smart Antenna techniques as applied to the introduction of Space Division Multiple Access (SDMA) techniques in current mobile radio networks, as well as in Personal Communication Services (PCS), Personal Communications Networks (PCN) and the Universal Mobile Telecommunication System (UMTS). It is shown qualitatively how SDMA techniques can increase the capacity of cellular network. Furthermore, a new SDMA principle based on the non-homogeneous Quality of Service requirements in mobile multi-media networks is introduced with application to systems proposed for UMTS.
